newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour must clarify windfall tax plan - Clarke.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour must clarify windfall tax plan - Clarke.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke on Thursday urged a parliamentary committee to demand that the opposition Labour Party make clear which privatised utilities would have to pay its proposed windfall profits tax.

Clarke's move followed evidence given to the Trade and Industry Committee on Wednesday by PowerGen Plc chairman Ed Wallis who said he understood from party leader Tony Blair's office that his company would not be liable for the tax.
Clarke said Blair or economics spokesman Gordon Brown should now "put out a clear statement saying which industries and which companies will pay this tax".
"They invented the tax and they should now describe it honestly," Clarke said in a statement.
"The Select Committee on Trade and Industry should call Gordon Brown before them and get him to answer the key questions for the benefit of the public, Powergen and the other utilities."
